problem: A developer working next to a coding agent has the design in one tool, the code in another, and no link between them. The agent reads a pull request diff and cannot tell which decision it violates; the person reads a decision and cannot tell which code implements it. Every tool in the loop assumes a human is the only author.
users: A solo developer building software next to a coding agent
A small team whose agents write most of the code and whose people own the design
A tool author shipping an app that mounts into the OpenKaava window
goals: One window holding the tools, the terminal, the files and the agent
Design and code in one repository, traced to each other by identifier
A tool protocol a third-party repository can be written against without reading the shell's source
Verification that an agent cannot talk its way past: build, test, lint and format, all four, every time
Every architectural decision written down once, with the alternative it rejected
non_goals: Running the software the user builds with it
A general-purpose code editor competing with VS Code on editing features
Sandboxing a plugin core — the tool protocol states plainly that it is unsandboxed
constraints: Windows first; the shell is Tauri over WebView2 and reaches it through the COM interface Tauri already holds
Rust owns everything that touches the machine; the frontend is a view over snapshots Rust produces
The three lint baselines are ratchets: they may shrink and may not grow
Port 1420 is the human's dev server and cannot be shared; agents use pnpm dev:agent
A failing test is never fixed by deleting or skipping the test
